figures.label: Figure 1
figures.caption: Preserved relationships and permitted changes in research-session exchange. (a–c) A representative source subgraph links a producing run and an assessment to a particular artifact version. The .science package carries native records, selected contents and RO-Crate metadata. Receiver identifiers may differ, while their mapped references must retain the corresponding targets. Symbols n, r and v denote illustrative identifiers, not measured record counts; the diagram omits other native record types. (d) The contract distinguishes object identity from payload availability, historical assessment outcomes from current scope applicability, and imported history from a writable fork. This is a design schematic rather than an additional experiment; the controlled observations appear in Figure 2.
figures.headline: Receiver identifiers may differ while mapped references keep their targets, and object identity stays separate from payload availability.

figures.label: Figure 2
figures.caption: Controlled revision trajectory and paired exchange conditions. (a) Three versions of summary.csv retain distinct assessment states. The initial version contains the intentional mean error; the corrected version has a corrective assessment; the subsequent revision carries an unreviewed fixture marker without a matching review scope. The disposition links the original finding to the corrective assessment without assigning that assessment to the unreviewed revision. The permutation test remains a recorded plan within the inspected trajectory. (b) Complete and partial exports originate from the same source session, with independently extracted snapshots serving as the audit reference. Both receiving projects retain the tested version and review associations; only the partial condition omits the unused note’s bytes and records that exclusion. Both imports use the same application installation. The dashed fork marks the operator’s editable-context observation for the complete import and the distinct saved session identity; it does not represent a new scientific analysis. The computational CSV’s required-evidence safeguard was an interface observation.
figures.headline: Three summary versions keep distinct assessment states, and both complete and partial imports retain the tested version and review associations.

figures.label: Figure S1
figures.caption: Case16 evidence associations and fixed-input re-execution. (a) Retained references associate trial_calculations.csv with a task message, a completed producing Notebook activity, a message snapshot and a scope-validated finding whose parent review includes the selected version. RO-Crate metadata also maps a file object to that version. Arrows gather these associations around the focal artifact; they do not assert an exhaustive causal graph. The package contains no native ArtifactVersionInput rows. (b) Offline execution of the retained analysis.py against registry_source.json under Python 3.12.14 reproduces the two saved CSV tables byte for byte. The retained calculation considers 93 candidates, excludes 13 and includes 80. These numbers describe this fixed-source calculation, not a fresh registry query or a model-performance evaluation. All 100 inventory entries of the supplied package passed size and checksum checks.

abstract: AI-assisted research leaves instructions, computations, artifact revisions and checks whose relationships matter when another researcher receives the work. We present AIPOCH Open-Science, an open-source research workbench with portable .science session packages, and specify an exchange contract for these recorded relationships. Version and assessment targets remain attributable while receiving-workspace identifiers can be remapped, eligible contents can be omitted explicitly, and imported history remains separate from a writable fork. A controlled session tested an incorrect first version, a reviewed correction, an unreviewed revision and a planned but unexecuted step. We compared complete and partial exports with source records extracted independently of the exporter, then inspected imports into separate projects within the same installation. Both conditions retained the tested version and review associations, kept the unreviewed revision distinct from earlier assessments and represented excluded content as unavailable. A documentation-rich ordinary directory also supplied evidence for all seven static inspection questions. A separate registry case connected a table to its recorded task, execution and review; offline execution of its retained script and fixed input reproduced two saved CSV tables byte for byte. The study contributes an implemented exchange contract and a controlled examination of its preservation rules, content-selection constraints and interpretation boundaries.

sections.body: This section lists the author affiliations, numbered in sequence. Most entries are hospitals, universities and research centers in China. Other entries are in Singapore (AIPOCH PTE. LTD. is listed first), the Netherlands, Israel, the United Kingdom and the United States, including a Boston hospital and an Illinois university. The section also contains the graphical abstract caption, which states that the work covers research tasks, persistent workbench records and reproducible .science packages for inspection and handoff. It reports no methods, results or limitations.
sections.heading: Author affiliations
sections.headline: The author list spans many hospitals and companies, mainly in China, with affiliations also in the Netherlands, Israel and the United States.

sections.body: The introduction states the problem: a shared AI-assisted result needs its task, executed activity, checked version and available materials to remain identifiable. It names three conflicts: a planned action without an execution record, a finding about an earlier version that does not assess a later revision, and selective file sharing that removes access to a payload. The authors propose an exchange contract implemented in AIPOCH Open-Science and examine it with a controlled trajectory containing an incorrect output, a reviewed correction, an unreviewed revision and an unexecuted plan, plus a registry case. The stated limits are that initial task attribution still needs surrounding conversation, observed file use does not establish a complete dependency graph, and a required-evidence control prevents some content exclusions.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Sharing AI-assisted research needs its task, version and review relations to survive transfer, not only the output files.

sections.body: This section places the work among existing systems. OpenAI4S is identified as the closest implemented precedent, combining persistent scientific execution, versioned artifacts and session exchange with quarantined read-only import. The authors cite PROV and P-Plan for separating plans from executions, AiiDA for export consistency, and RO-Crate and Workflow Run RO-Crate for packaging and execution description. Agent-provenance and artifact-observability systems are cited for artifact identifiers and claim–evidence bindings. The section states that the evaluation tests the contract within AIPOCH Open-Science and does not compare the two systems experimentally, and that certification against Workflow Run profiles was outside the present evaluation.
sections.heading: Related work
sections.headline: Earlier provenance and session-sharing systems cover parts of the problem; this work focuses on version and review attribution after exchange.

sections.body: This section defines the evaluation and implementation. Session records are typed objects and relations mapped to native fields. The exporter uses an explicit table allowlist and traverses earlier versions, upstream inputs, findings, owning reviews and referenced versions until no required object is missing; missing required evidence causes failure. Eligible immutable payloads can be excluded only when their storage key, filename and size match and their bytes do not occur in retained evidence. A .science file is a gzip-compressed tar archive with manifest.json, session.json, records.json and ro-crate-metadata.json. Import remaps identifiers, keeps history read-only and opens a writable fork. Controlled operations used Open-Science 0.37.1 on macOS, and the paired validation protocol was frozen before the application run.
sections.heading: Methods and implementation
sections.headline: The method maps workbench records into typed objects and relations, then checks an exported package against an independently extracted source reference.

sections.body: Results cover the controlled session and the case16 example. The final controlled source held three artifact lineages and six artifact versions, with two reviews, two findings, two review-scope snapshots and one finding disposition. The failed finding stayed bound to the first version, and no scope assessed the final revision. Complete and partial exports each matched 138 source comparisons, and each receiver matched 146 mapped comparisons and both held 28 messages. In the partial condition, the unused note's bytes were omitted with an explicit descriptor, while the computational CSV was protected as required evidence in the interface. The case16 package contained zero native ArtifactVersionInput rows. A table-to-task, run and review query was answered from retained references, and offline re-execution reproduced two saved tables byte for byte. An ordinary documentation-rich directory located evidence for all seven static questions.
sections.heading: Results
sections.headline: Relations, not just files, survived export in a controlled session, with all paired comparisons matching in both exchange conditions.

sections.body: The discussion draws design lessons and states boundaries. An earlier failed assessment, a corrective assessment and the lack of a check on a new revision can all be true together, so exchange must keep the targets of historical judgments separate from current scope. For partial sharing, the authors propose a conditional rule: represent eligible omissions explicitly and refuse selections that conflict with inseparable retained evidence. The records cannot turn a contextual association into a causal dependency, since task attribution still required reading the conversation. The outdated labels observed on historical review cards remain unexplained, because the saved evidence lacks before-and-after interface states. The main test used one trajectory and two projects in one installation, and source capture completeness is unmeasured.
sections.heading: Discussion
sections.headline: A failed assessment, its correction and an unreviewed revision can all be true together, so exchange must keep each target separate.

sections.body: The conclusion summarizes the contract: recorded version and assessment relations survive local identifier mapping and explicit omission of eligible contents. In a controlled same-installation trajectory, the tested relations were retained through complete and partial exchange, an unreviewed revision was kept distinct from earlier checks, and a separate writable fork was produced. The case16 inspection linked a scientific table to its recorded task, execution and review, and a fixed-input run reproduced two saved tables byte for byte. The authors state that the scope is the tested records and operations, and that broader capture completeness and recipient outcomes require further evaluation.
sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.headline: The contract keeps recorded version and review relations across identifier mapping and explicit omissions, with evidence limited to the tested records.

sections.body: This section gives access locations. AIPOCH Open-Science is available under the Apache License 2.0 on GitHub, and the official website and the public research-case collection on Hugging Face are listed. The evaluated case16 snapshot is identified in the validation release by separate integrity records, not by the collection's current main branch. The AIPOCH-AI/case-validation release on Hugging Face is described as versioned and de-identified, and includes protocols, source snapshots, packages, import receipts, comparisons, the ordinary-directory control, the operator's fork report, offline auditors and a fixed-input rerun. Identifiers are aliased and local paths replaced, so application observations concern the original records while renewed audits check the publication copies.
sections.heading: Data and code availability
sections.headline: The software is released under Apache 2.0, and a de-identified validation release on Hugging Face contains the protocol, packages and audit scripts.

sections.body: This declaration states that Codex (OpenAI) assisted with literature retrieval, source-code inspection, application operation, evidence organization, manuscript revision, validation code and offline re-execution. It refers to the Methods and supporting materials for the scope of these activities. The authors state that they are responsible for checking sources, interpreting findings and reviewing the submitted text and materials.
sections.heading: Declaration of AI assistance
sections.headline: Codex assisted with literature retrieval, source inspection, application operation and validation code, and the authors remain responsible for interpretation.
